The one open question is a scope question routed to the Phase 2 interview rather than to N blind prep candidates — candidates cannot answer 'does Dalton want the sibling endpoint in this ticket'.
synthesis: DEV-2232 guarded the shift-START side effect (lazy kit_shifts create + ShiftStart analytics/audit) in ClarityScoutShiftController::status() behind an isScoutForceImpersonator() check, and deliberately left end() untouched. end() (POST /api/scout/shift/end) has the mirror-image bug: it fires Analytics::track(ShiftEnd) unconditionally before doing any work, and its idempotent-close logic falls back to EnsureOpenShift::forKit($kit) when no shift exists — so an impersonating admin who taps End Shift creates a zero-activity kit_shifts row, closes it, dispatches SendEndOfShiftSummary, writes a 'Scout shift ended' audit row, and fires a ShiftEnd analytics event, purely as a side effect of impersonation. Fix: add the same isScoutForceImpersonator() short-circuit to end(), after the '! $kit' 403 check and before any Analytics::track or DB work.

scope.summary: Add an isScoutForceImpersonator() guard to ClarityScoutShiftController::end() that returns immediately (no KitShift read/write, no Analytics::track, no audit log, no SendEndOfShiftSummary dispatch) for a force-login impersonator, mirroring the shipped status() guard from DEV-2232.

proposed_changes.change: In end(), after the `if (! $kit)` 403 block and before `Analytics::track(ScoutAnalyticsEvent::ShiftEnd->value, ...)`, add an `if ($user->isScoutForceImpersonator())` early return of `['data' => ['shift_id' => null, 'open' => false, 'started_at' => null, 'ended_at' => null, 'end_type' => null, 'newly_closed' => false]]`.
proposed_changes.reason: Mirrors the DEV-2232 precedent in status() and blocks the same side-effect class (lazy KitShift create/close, Analytics::track, activity-log write, summary-job dispatch) for the end-shift path.

proposed_changes.change: Update the class docblock's 'Both endpoints lazily materialize...' note so the documented contract reflects that BOTH endpoints now carry the impersonator exception.
proposed_changes.reason: The docblock currently documents only status()'s exception; leaving it would make the class's own contract wrong.

proposed_changes.change: In logout(), gate ONLY the Analytics::track(Logout) call behind `! $user->isScoutForceImpersonator()`. Do NOT early-return: `$request->user()->currentAccessToken()->delete()` must still run so the impersonator's force token is revoked and impersonation exits. Resolve `$user = $request->user()` once and evaluate the predicate BEFORE the delete, since isScoutForceImpersonator() reads currentAccessToken().
proposed_changes.reason: Same defect class as end(): a force-login impersonator exiting impersonation writes a driver-attributed Logout analytics event. Graded `buggy` by the exhaustiveness sweep; scope-expanded into this ticket by Dalton at the Phase 2 gate.

out_of_scope: ClarityScoutNotificationsController::markRead()/markAllRead() and ClarityScoutScanDispositionController — explicit user-initiated writes, graded `safe`: they are the impersonator deliberately acting as the driver, not an implicit/lazy side effect of merely being logged in.
CloseInactiveShiftsCommand — scheduled, not request-scoped, no impersonator context.

The session('impersonator') vs session('admin_impersonator') key mismatch between ClarityScoutShiftController::logShiftActivity() and the Scout force-login flow — pre-existing unrelated drift; flagged, not fixed (CLAUDE.md: do not silently fix unrelated drift).

A normal driver's end-shift behavior is unchanged.

acceptance_criteria.reason: resources/js/clarity-scout/composables/useShift.js:64-94 endShift() reads every field with optional chaining + fallbacks (data?.shift_id ?? shiftId.value, data?.started_at ?? startedAt.value, data?.ended_at ?? new Date().toISOString(), data?.end_type ?? 'confirmed') and never reads newly_closed — so a fully-null payload carrying the full key set is safe.

acceptance_criteria.reason: Dalton elected to fix the sibling defect in this ticket rather than defer it.

questions.q: The exhaustiveness sweep graded a sibling site buggy: ClarityScoutAuthController::logout() fires Analytics::track(Logout) unconditionally and is reachable by a force token. Fix it in this ticket, or exclude it (and, if excluded, does Dalton want a follow-up DEV ticket opened for it)?
questions.answer: Fix BOTH in this ticket. Dalton chose to guard ClarityScoutAuthController::logout() alongside end(). Note the shapes differ: end() early-returns entirely, whereas logout() must STILL revoke the token (that is how the impersonator exits) and only skip the Analytics::track(Logout) call. The predicate reads currentAccessToken(), so the check must run BEFORE the token delete.

questions.q: Should the impersonator branch of end() return status()'s fully-null payload, or end()'s own key set with nulled values plus newly_closed:false?
questions.answer: end()'s own key set with nulled values + newly_closed:false. The existing response-shape lock test asserts end() responses carry newly_closed as a structural key, and the PWA consumer (useShift.js:64-94) never reads newly_closed and optional-chains every other field with a fallback.

questions.q: Does isScoutForceImpersonator() key on anything besides the Sanctum token ability?
questions.answer: No. It is a single exact-membership check: in_array('clarity-scout-force', $this->currentAccessToken()?->abilities ?? [], true) at app/Models/User.php:252 — deliberately not tokenCan(), because a normal token's '*' ability would falsely satisfy that.

questions.q: Is EnsureOpenShift::forKit() reachable from anywhere besides end()?
questions.answer: Not directly — end() (ClarityScoutShiftController.php:130) is its only external caller. currentOpenForKit() calls it internally, and that path is already impersonator-guarded upstream in status().

questions.q: Should the audit-log write be suppressed too, not just analytics?
questions.answer: Yes — the ticket's Expected section says 'should not emit ShiftEnd analytics/audit'. Returning before the transaction suppresses both by construction, as status()'s guard does.

questions.q: okf/concepts/scout-shifts-and-trips.md documents the CURRENT end() behavior ('ShiftEnd fires unconditionally', 'the audit row IS written during impersonation'). Does this fix make that page stale, and should it be corrected now?
questions.answer: Yes, both lines go stale. The correction is QUEUED, not made now: CLAUDE.md's OKF WRITE rule forbids writing to okf/ while work is in flight — wiki edits land only after the change is merged or has passed final review/QA. Recorded in notes[] and carried to the Build Record.

notes: okf/concepts/scout-shifts-and-trips.md's Observability section documents pre-fix end() behavior on two counts; queue the correction for the post-approval wiki pass.

logShiftActivity() reads session('impersonator') while the Scout force-login flow sets session('admin_impersonator') — a pre-existing key mismatch meaning the _impersonator property on the confirmed-end audit row is likely never populated today. Unrelated drift; flagged only.

status() and end() will each carry a duplicated literal isScoutForceImpersonator() block. Extracting a private helper would DRY it, but the shipped status() precedent did not extract one; matching the precedent is the smaller, more consistent change. Note the duplication is intentional in the PR.

SCOPE EXPANDED at the Phase 2 gate (human answer): logout() joined end(). The two guards are deliberately DIFFERENT shapes — end() early-returns; logout() gates only the analytics call and still revokes the token. A reviewer seeing asymmetry should read this note before flagging it.

tests.what_it_pins: New sibling to the DEV-2232 test status_does_not_open_a_shift_or_track_shift_start_for_a_force_login_impersonator: with a clarity-scout-force token, POST /api/scout/shift/end must assert 200, assertDatabaseCount('kit_shifts', 0), no ShiftEnd Analytics::track call, no 'Scout shift ended' activity_log row, and Queue::assertNotPushed(SendEndOfShiftSummary::class). Plus the impersonator response still carrying the full data.{shift_id,open,started_at,ended_at,end_type,newly_closed} key set. MUST NOT be class-level RequiresClickhouse-gated (that silently skips in normal CI).

With a clarity-scout-force token, POST /api/scout/logout must assert 200, no Logout Analytics::track call, AND that the token IS revoked (the impersonator can still exit) — the revocation assertion is the load-bearing half, because an early-return implementation would strand the impersonator. Plus a normal-driver logout test proving the Logout event still fires. Existing force-token references live at lines 211, 322, 361.
